groups.text: It is currently 18 degrees with showers in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

At least 48 people are dead after a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck the Indonesian island of Florès. Thousands of evacuees are now waiting for aid, with some regions left without electricity or telecommunications and at least one emergency access road remaining impassable. Rescue workers in Maumere are searching through damaged buildings as nearly 5,000 people have been forced from their homes. In a separate shift toward specialized technology, Artificial Analysis has released a new platform called Optima. The tool allows users to build custom AI benchmarks using their own data and workflows rather than relying on general-purpose public tests. By tailoring these benchmarks to specific use cases, users can compare leading models based on quality, cost per task, and time per task. This approach aims to reveal which models work best for individual business applications where raw token pricing may not provide a complete picture.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that Russia has lost approximately 1,467,320 troops since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. This total includes 1,510 casualties suffered by Russian forces over the past day alone. The material toll is equally steep, with losses including 12,270 tanks, 25,151 armored combat vehicles, and 47,007 artillery systems. Russia has also lost 134,851 vehicles and fuel tanks, along with over 463,000 unmanned aerial vehicles. While Ukraine maintains operational secrecy regarding its own losses, the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimates a casualty ratio of roughly 2.5 to 1 or 2 to 1 in favor of Ukraine. A report from January 2026 suggests Ukrainian casualties likely fall between 500,000 and 600,000. These figures highlight the immense scale of attrition as both nations continue to fight for control of the region.

Thousands of evacuees on Indonesia's Flores island began receiving aid Sunday after a 7.7-magnitude earthquake killed 48 people and injured dozens. The quake damaged hundreds of buildings and forced some 5,000 residents to flee their homes, while others were left without telecommunications or electricity. In contrast, the Pacific is facing a different crisis as Category 1 Hurricane Lala brings destructive winds and massive rainfall to Hawaii's Big Island. The National Hurricane Center warned of landslides and life-threatening floods, prompting the closure of several airports and the suspension of public transit. Hawaiian Electric reports that power lines and poles were damaged across nearly 70 kilometers, leaving tens of thousands of households without electricity. While Indonesia deals with the aftermath of a sudden seismic event, residents on Big Island are being told to remain in safe shelters as the storm continues its path.

The 60-day deadline for negotiations between the United States and Iran expires this weekend. This memorandum was intended to resolve the atomic dispute or reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but it has since lost its significance. Meanwhile, in Washington, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt is stepping down from her post. In North Africa, a different tension persists regarding the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. Two weeks after a mass arrival of migrants, fears of another surge have not been confirmed. However, the Spanish newspaper ABC argues that these illegal border crossings are an attack on the state's foundations rather than simple administrative failure. The publication claims migration is being used as a tool for blackmail against Spain. ABC asserts that while the military has the constitutional mandate to defend territorial integrity, the central government has failed to activate the necessary security instruments.

Tensions are rising in Osun State as misinformation spreads alongside reports of police volatility during the election period. In Modakeke, Ife East, a video circulated showing police officers storming a Registration Area Centre and firing tear gas. While some reports claimed officers disrupted the distribution of materials or stole them, the Osun State Police Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, clarified that an officer accidentally discharged the gas and has since been apprehended. He denied that any election materials were taken. Meanwhile, separate claims on X and Facebook alleged that police arrested fake collation agents and observers linked to the Accord Party in Ila Orangun on August 14. However, fact-checkers found these reports misleading. Because collation officers are not operational until election day, arrests for those roles on the eve of the vote are procedurally inconsistent, and no credible evidence links the individuals in the video to the Accord Party.

Intelligence agencies report that North Korea is preparing to send up to 50,000 additional troops to Russia. This follows an initial deployment of roughly 14,000 to 15,000 soldiers in late 2024 to defend the Kursk region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warns that this expanded military cooperation, which includes North Korean ballistic missiles being fired from Russian territory, threatens security across Ukraine and the Asia-Pacific. While some experts believe these forces will primarily secure border areas like Voronezh to free up Russian troops for front lines in Kharkiv or Sumy, others doubt the move will fundamentally change the war's course. Meanwhile, in Western Europe, Belgium is battling one of the worst wildfires in its modern history. The blaze broke out Friday in the High Fens nature reserve near the German border, jumping from 80 hectares to over 2,700 hectares in just twenty-four hours. The EU has scrambled water bombers and helicopters as hundreds of villagers evacuate.

Extreme drought is gripping much of Germany this summer, leaving plants across the country under severe water stress. Along the banks of the Rhine in Bonn, dry leaves already crunch underfoot and tree crowns have turned yellow or gone completely bald. This loss is critical because large, leafy trees act as natural air conditioners for urban areas, keeping temperatures under a canopy up to three degrees cooler than the surrounding environment. In cities, however, concrete and asphalt prevent rain from soaking into the soil, instead funneling water directly into the sewers. To survive the heat, trees close the pores in their leaves to prevent water loss, but this mechanism slows photosynthesis and causes the plants to starve. As these urban cooling systems fail, city centers face the risk of becoming even hotter.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 20 and 24 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the summer holidays in Berlin and the holiday of Assumption Day.
Mail worth checking: ChatGPT sent an update that your Weekly Article Pick task has been paused.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
